slides.say: a and b are integers. a is odd, and b is even and not zero. Which of the following is the most precise description of six a over b squared?

So the top of the fraction, six a, is even, and the bottom of the fraction, b squared, is even too. But even over even does not decide whether the answer is an integer. We need to use the particular factors in this fraction. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, simplifying the factors first, and then plugging in numbers.

[short pause] Let's start by simplifying. b is even and not zero, so write b as two times an integer k. k cannot be zero either. To square b, square the whole product, two times k. Two squared is four, so b squared is four k squared. Our fraction is six a over four k squared. Divide the top and bottom by two. We get three a over two k squared.

Now look at the simpler fraction. a is odd, so three a is odd. The bottom, two k squared, is even. It has a two that cannot cancel with the odd top. So the fraction cannot give an integer. It is always a fraction that is not a whole number, and choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: This is why we simplified first. There was a two in the six on top, and it cancelled with one two on the bottom. But another two stayed on the bottom, and it cannot cancel with the odd number on top.

[pause] Now let's try plugging in. a must be odd, and b must be even and nonzero. Use a is one and b is two. Six a is six, and b squared is four, so the result is six over four, or three over two. It is not an integer. Now check the choices. Every description includes a fraction, so this example does not separate them. Getting another fraction would not separate them either.

We need the most precise description, so ask whether an integer could ever occur. As we saw when simplifying, b is two k, and the fraction becomes three a over two k squared. The top is odd and the bottom is even. The two on the bottom cannot cancel with the odd top, so the result cannot be an integer. It is always a non-integer fraction. Choice number two is our answer. This short rule settles what more examples would not. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: two on the bottom cannot cancel
Choice number two is our answer
